messages:
alex: seeing apiserver 503 spike in us-west-2 starting ~09:12 UTC. kube-apiserver errors spike, lots of attach/provisioner failures mixed in.

maria: checking etcd metrics now — put latency up to ~2.1s, wal fsync latency high on etcd-3. nvme/io wait saturated on leader.

jonathan: controller-manager logs show thrashing: requeues for AttachVolume and Node status updates. Provisioner returning 429s. backlog growing.

sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-042 - control-plane-io-surge-usw2 (severity=high) :rotating_light:

alex: can we divert traffic to eu-west for a quick relief? we have spare capacity there.

priya: failover has risk — leader election already flapping a bit. if we move API traffic we need to ensure endpoints and cert SANs ok.

maria: quick mitigation plan: pause heavy etcd compaction jobs, and bump etcd disk IOPS (temp) on the leader. options: increase gp3 iops or attach local nvme.

jonathan: also consider reducing apiserver fanout: set --max-requests-inflight and lower watch burst settings temporarily. watch cache exploding is contributing.

alex: running volume modification now (aws CLI):
```
aws ec2 modify-volume --volume-id vol-0abcd1234efgh --iops 8000 --throughput 500
```

maria: applied change on etcd-3 leader, IOPS metrics show ~7.8k now, wal fsync latencies dropping from ~800ms to ~90ms.

devops: applied smart-routing: divert ~20% API traffic to eu-west region via routing policy. monitoring propagation.

jonathan: controller-manager requeues down substantially. attach failure rate: 120/min -> 3/min. provisioning backlog is clearing.

priya: we should capture cost delta — temporary iops bump costs ~+$0.25/hr for that volume, plus cross-region routing impact. note for postmortem.

alex: nice work. opening a postmortem doc and action items now. :thumbsup:

maria: action items (initial): [1] add rate-limiter/staggering to GPU onboarding pipeline, owner: alex; [2] stagger etcd compaction windows across clusters, owner: priya; [3] add telemetry for wal fsync + alert threshold, owner: maria; [4] perf test local NVMe for etcd leader, owner: jonathan.

alex: ack, I'll create the doc and schedule follow-up. tagging @oncall for visibility.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-2026-042 status: mitigated — system metrics stable for 15m. continuing to monitor. :white_check_mark:

maria: leaving monitoring for another hour, then we'll transition to RCA writeup.

jonathan: postmortem checklist noted. I'll include logs and controller-manager requeue graphs.

priya: note — if we expect sustained onboarding spikes, we should evaluate pre-warming etcd nodes with higher baseline IOPS or use local NVMe class for control-plane volumes.

alex: agreed. thanks team.
